title: Why Does the Thermostat Say Cool but the AC Is Not Running?

seo.title: Thermostat Says Cool but AC Is Not Running: What to Check
seo.meta_description: If the thermostat says it is cooling but the AC does not run, check the normal delay, power, filter, indoor/outdoor units, and signs of coil icing.
seo.search_intent: Diagnose a thermostat showing a cooling call when the air-conditioning system is not actually producing cooling.

excerpt: If the display says “Cool On,” the thermostat believes it has requested cooling. The next useful question is which part of the system started: indoor fan, outdoor unit, both, or neither.
content_html:
Listen and observe before resetting anything. Knowing whether the indoor blower and outdoor unit are running separates several fault paths.

Allow the normal compressor-protection delay

After a mode change or power restoration, many systems wait several minutes before starting the compressor. Do not repeatedly move the setpoint up and down.

If nothing runs

Check equipment power, service switches, and the filter. Some systems also have condensate safety switches that stop cooling when a drain problem raises water level.

If air moves but it is not cool

See whether the outdoor unit is operating. A tripped breaker can be reset once; if it trips again, leave the system off.

If you see ice, stop forcing cooling

Restricted airflow and other faults can freeze the evaporator. Turn off cooling and allow thawing according to the manual; do not chip ice from the coil.

Know the homeowner limit

Do not open electrical panels or handle refrigerant. An outdoor unit that will not start, hums, repeatedly trips protection, or a system that re-freezes needs qualified service.

“The thermostat is calling for cooling” does not prove the AC is delivering it; identify which stage failed to follow the call.

faq.question: Why does Cool On show before the AC starts?
faq.answer: Many thermostats use a several-minute compressor protection delay.

faq.question: What should I do if the coil is iced?
faq.answer: Stop cooling, allow thawing as the manual directs, check the filter, and get service if icing returns.

faq.question: Can I recharge refrigerant myself?
faq.answer: No. Refrigerant problems require qualified diagnosis and service.
